After a refresh, the account page shows the light theme instead of the saved dark theme. The part that sets a starting theme runs after the saved choice arrives and overwrites it, so this is a real bug (the default-theme initializer, `src/profile-theme.ts:62`; the profile service returns "dark", yet `node --test test/profile-theme.test.mjs` shows dark becoming light). Skipping that starting theme after a saved one loads is a small, safe fix, so the hotfix is recommended below.

- The account page writes the theme twice. It first loads the saved theme from the profile service, which returns `{"theme":"dark"}`, and applies it. A separate default-theme initializer runs later and sets `"light"`.
- The local test `node --test test/profile-theme.test.mjs` reproduces the report. After a refresh the expected theme is dark and the observed theme is light.
- The leading hypothesis is that the later default initializer overwrites the saved theme. The falsification test ran: with the later initializer disabled, dark is retained, which supports this hypothesis.
- No other ranked hypothesis was needed to explain the overwrite. No prior reader context explains why the page has two competing theme writers.
- The prior-report search completed across open and closed issues and found no match.
- The smallest fix is to skip default initialization once a saved theme has loaded. All six hotfix predicates pass.
